<p id="mwCQ"><b id="mwCg">ESP32</b> is a family of low-cost, energy-efficient <a data-relay-id="e119" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microcontroller" id="mwCw" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Microcontroller">microcontrollers</a> that support both <a data-relay-id="e120" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wi-Fi" id="mwDA" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Wi-Fi">Wi-Fi</a> and <a data-relay-id="e121" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluetooth" id="mwDQ" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Bluetooth">Bluetooth</a>. These chips feature several processing options, including the <a data-relay-id="e122" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tensilica" id="mwDg" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Tensilica">Tensilica</a> Xtensa LX6 microprocessor available in dual-core and single-core variants, the Xtensa LX7 dual-core processor, or a <a data-relay-id="e123" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RISC-V" id="mwDw" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="RISC-V">RISC-V</a> microprocessor. The ESP32 incorporates components for wireless data communication such as built-in antenna switches, an RF <a data-relay-id="e124" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balun" id="mwEA" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Balun">balun</a>, power amplifiers, low-noise receivers, filters, and power-management modules.</p>
<p id="mwEQ">Typically, the ESP32 is embedded on device-specific <a data-relay-id="e125" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Printed_circuit_board" id="mwEg" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Printed circuit board">printed circuit boards</a> (PCBs) or offered as part of development kits that include a variety of <a class="mw-redirect" data-relay-id="e126" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPIO" id="mwEw" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="GPIO">GPIO</a> pins and connectors, with configurations varying by model and manufacturer. The ESP32 was designed by <a data-relay-id="e127" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espressif_Systems" id="mwFA" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Espressif Systems">Espressif Systems</a> and is manufactured by <a data-relay-id="e128" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSMC" id="mwFQ" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="TSMC">TSMC</a> using their 40<span id="mwFg" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>nm process.<sup about="#mwt12" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"EspressifESP32ProductPage"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-EspressifESP32ProductPage-2"}}' id="cite_ref-EspressifESP32ProductPage_2-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e129" href="#cite_note-EspressifESP32ProductPage-2" id="mwFw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwGA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGQ">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwGg">]</span></span></a></sup> It is a successor to the <a data-relay-id="e130" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESP8266" id="mwGw" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="ESP8266">ESP8266</a> microcontroller.</p>
<meta data-mw='{"autoGenerated":true}' id="mwHA" property="mw:PageProp/toc"/></section><section aria-labelledby="Features" data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwHQ"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Features">Features</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a data-relay-id="e131" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ESP32&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Features"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" id="mwHg" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a class="mw-file-description" data-relay-id="e132" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ESP32-Dieshot.jpg" id="mwHw"><img class="mw-file-element" data-file-height="5318" data-file-type="bitmap" data-file-width="5518" decoding="async" height="241" id="mwIA" loading="lazy" resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ESP32-Dieshot.jpg" src="assets/152f9432945ebb4cc5bb7f85.jpg" width="250"/></a><figcaption id="mwIQ">ESP32 <a data-relay-id="e133" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die_shot" id="mwIg" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Die shot">die shot</a>. Most of the chip area is covered by a <a data-relay-id="e134" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_network_design_(IC)" id="mwIw" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Power network design (IC)">power distribution network</a> on the top metal layers.</figcaption></figure><p id="mwJA">Since the release of the original ESP32, a number of variants have been introduced and announced. They form the ESP32 family of microcontrollers.<sup about="#mwt15" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-3"}}' id="cite_ref-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e135" href="#cite_note-3" id="mwJQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwJg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJw">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKA">]</span></span></a></sup> These chips have different CPUs and capabilities, but all share the same SDK and are largely code-compatible. Additionally, the original ESP32 was revised (see ESP32 ECO V3,esp 32 cam</p>
<p id="mwKQ">for example).

</section><section aria-labelledby="QFN_packaged_chip_and_module" data-mw-section-id="2" id="mwAW4"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="QFN_packaged_chip_and_module">QFN packaged chip and module</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a data-relay-id="e149" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ESP32&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: QFN packaged chip and module"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" id="mwAW8" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a class="mw-file-description" data-relay-id="e150" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ESP32-S3_on_paper.jpg" id="mwAXA"><img class="mw-file-element" data-file-height="3000" data-file-type="bitmap" data-file-width="3000" decoding="async" height="250" id="mwAXE" loading="lazy" resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ESP32-S3_on_paper.jpg" src="assets/526d15988834f45b60b51c8c.jpg" width="250"/></a><figcaption id="mwAXI">ESP32-S3-Wroom-1 board</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwAXM">ESP32 is housed in <a class="mw-redirect" data-relay-id="e151" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quad_flat_no-leads_package" id="mwAXQ" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Quad flat no-leads package">quad-flat no-leads</a> (QFN) packages of varying sizes with 49 pads. Specifically, 48 connection pads along the sides and one large thermal pad (connected to ground) on the bottom.</p>
<section aria-labelledby="Chips" data-mw-section-id="3" id="mwAXU"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Chips">Chips</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a data-relay-id="e152" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ESP32&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Chips"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" id="mwAXY" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a class="mw-file-description" data-relay-id="e153" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ESP32-C3_RISC-V_NodeMCU_board.jpg" id="mwAXc"><img class="mw-file-element" data-file-height="2673" data-file-type="bitmap" data-file-width="1683" decoding="async" height="397" id="mwAXg" loading="lazy" resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ESP32-C3_RISC-V_NodeMCU_board.jpg" src="assets/ed3bd56468e2188770db22e4.jpg" width="250"/></a><figcaption id="mwAXk"><a data-relay-id="e154" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NodeMCU" id="mwAXo" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="NodeMCU">NodeMCU</a> board with an ESP32-C3-32S</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwAXs">The ESP32 <a data-relay-id="e155" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System_on_a_chip" id="mwAXw" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="System on a chip">system on a chip</a> integrated circuit is packaged in both 6<span id="mwAX0" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>mm × 6<span id="mwAX4" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>mm and 5<span id="mwAX8" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>mm × 5<span id="mwAYA" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>mm sized QFN packages.</p>

<p id="mwApM">In 2020, chips ESP32-D0WDQ6 and ESP32-D0WD also got a V3 version (ESP32 ECO V3), which fixes some of the bugs<sup about="#mwt27" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"ESP32bugs"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-ESP32bugs-5"}}' id="cite_ref-ESP32bugs_5-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e160" href="#cite_note-ESP32bugs-5" id="mwApQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwApU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwApY">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwApc">]</span></span></a></sup> and introduces improvements over the previous versions.</p>
</section><section aria-labelledby="Modules" data-mw-section-id="4" id="mwApg"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Modules">Modules</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a data-relay-id="e161" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ESP32&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Modules"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwApk">The ESP32 PICO <a class="mw-redirect" data-relay-id="e162" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System_in_package" id="mwApo" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="System in package">system in package</a> modules combine an ESP32 silicon chip, crystal oscillator, flash memory chip, filter capacitors, and RF matching links into a single 7<span id="mwAps" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>mm × 7<span id="mwApw" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>mm sized QFN package.</p>
<p id="mwAp0">The first released PICO was the ESP32-PICO-D4 with 2 CPUs at 240<span id="mwAp4" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MHz, 4MiB internal flash, a 40<span id="mwAp8" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MHz oscillator and 34 GPIOs.<sup about="#mwt30" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-6"}}' id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e163" href="#cite_note-6" id="mwAqA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAqE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAqI">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAqM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<p id="mwAqQ">Later, in 2020, the ESP32-PICO-V3 and ESP32-PICO-V3-02 modules were introduced both based on the ESP32 ECO V3 wafer.<sup about="#mwt33" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-7"}}' id="cite_ref-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e164" href="#cite_note-7" id="mwAqU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAqY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAqc">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAqg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt36" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-8"}}' id="cite_ref-8" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e165" href="#cite_note-8" id="mwAqk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAqo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAqs">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAqw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<p id="mwAq0">In 2022 the ESP32-S3-PICO-1 module was introduced with USB OTG and internal PSRAM.<sup about="#mwt39" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-9"}}' id="cite_ref-9" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e166" href="#cite_note-9" id="mwAq4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAq8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwArA">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwArE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section><section aria-labelledby="Printed_circuit_boards" data-mw-section-id="5" id="mwAuQ"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Printed_circuit_boards">Printed circuit boards</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a data-relay-id="e170" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ESP32&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Printed circuit boards"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<section aria-labelledby="Surface-mount_module_boards" data-mw-section-id="6" id="mwAuU"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Surface-mount_module_boards">Surface-mount module boards</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a data-relay-id="e171" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ESP32&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Surface-mount module boards"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwAuY">ESP32 based <a data-relay-id="e172" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface-mount_technology" id="mwAuc" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Surface-mount technology">surface-mount</a> <a data-relay-id="e173" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Printed_circuit_board" id="mwAug" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Printed circuit board">printed circuit board</a> modules directly contain the ESP32 <a data-relay-id="e174" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System_on_a_chip" id="mwAuk" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="System on a chip">SoC</a> and are designed to be easily integrated onto other circuit boards. Meandered <a data-relay-id="e175" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverted-F_antenna" id="mwAuo" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Inverted-F antenna">inverted-F antenna</a> designs are used for the PCB trace antennas on the modules listed below. In addition to flash memory, some modules include <a class="mw-redirect" data-relay-id="e176" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSRAM" id="mwAus" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="PSRAM">pseudostatic RAM</a> (pSRAM).</p>

<tr id="mwAyI">
<td id="mwAyM">ESP32-WROOM-32E</td>
<td id="mwAyQ" style="text-align:center">4,8,16</td>
<td id="mwAyU">Same as ESP32-WROOM-32 but with the Eco V3 processor revisions<sup about="#mwt70" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"EspressifModules"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-EspressifModules-19"}}' id="cite_ref-EspressifModules_19-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e187" href="#cite_note-EspressifModules-19" id="mwAyY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAyc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAyg">[</span>19<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAyk">]</span></span></a></sup></td></tr>
<tr id="mwAyo">
<td id="mwAys">ESP32-WROOM-32D</td>
<td id="mwAyw" rowspan="7" style="text-align:center">4</td>
<td id="mwAy0">Revision of the ESP-WROOM-32 module which uses an ESP32-D0WD chip instead of an ESP32-D0WDQ6 chip.<sup about="#mwt73" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"EspressifESPWROOM32DUDatasheet"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-EspressifESPWROOM32DUDatasheet-20"}}' id="cite_ref-EspressifESPWROOM32DUDatasheet_20-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e188" href="#cite_note-EspressifESPWROOM32DUDatasheet-20" id="mwAy4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAy8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAzA">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAzE">]</span></span></a></sup> Originally named "ESP-WROOM-32D".</td></tr>
<tr id="mwAzI">
<td id="mwAzM">ESP32-SOLO-1</td>
<td id="mwAzQ">Similar to the ESP32-WROOM-32D module, but uses the single-core ESP32-S0WD chip instead of the dual-core ESP32-D0WD.</td></tr>
<tr id="mwAzU">
<td id="mwAzY"><span about="#mwt74" class="nowrap" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"nowrap","href":"./Template:Nowrap"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"ESP32-WROOM-32U"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwAzc" typeof="mw:Transclusion">ESP32-WROOM-32U</span></td>
<td id="mwAzg"><a data-relay-id="e189" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hirose_U.FL" id="mwAzk" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Hirose U.FL">U.FL socket</a></td>
<td id="mwAzo">Alternative to the ESP-WROOM-32D module which has a U.FL connector for external antenna in lieu of a PCB trace antenna.<sup about="#mwt75" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"EspressifESPWROOM32DUDatasheet"}}' id="cite_ref-EspressifESPWROOM32DUDatasheet_20-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e190" href="#cite_note-EspressifESPWROOM32DUDatasheet-20" id="mwAzs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAzw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAz0">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAz4">]</span></span></a></sup></td></tr>
<tr id="mwAz8">
<td id="mwA0A"><span about="#mwt76" class="nowrap" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"nowrap","href":"./Template:Nowrap"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"ESP32-WROVER"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwA0E" typeof="mw:Transclusion">ESP32-WROVER</span></td>
<td id="mwA0I">PCB trace</td>
<td id="mwA0M" rowspan="2" style="text-align:center">4</td>
<td id="mwA0Q">ESP32 module board with 4<span id="mwA0U" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MiB pSRAM created by Espressif. FCC part 15.247 tested (FCC ID 2AC7Z-ESP32WROVER). Uses 40<span id="mwA0Y" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MHz crystal oscillator. Does not include U.FL connector. Based on ESP32-D0WDQ6 chip. Since June 2018, new modules have been upgraded to 8<span id="mwA0c" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MiB pSRAM.</td></tr>
<tr id="mwA0g">
<td id="mwA0k"><span about="#mwt77" class="nowrap" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"nowrap","href":"./Template:Nowrap"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"ESP32-WROVER-I"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwA0o" typeof="mw:Transclusion">ESP32-WROVER-I</span></td>
<td id="mwA0s">U.FL socket, PCB trace</td>
<td id="mwA0w">Variation of ESP32-WROVER module configured to use an on-board U.FL compatible connector. PCB trace antenna not connected by default.</td></tr>
<tr id="mwA00">
<td id="mwA04"><span about="#mwt78" class="nowrap" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"nowrap","href":"./Template:Nowrap"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"ESP32-WROVER-B"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwA08" typeof="mw:Transclusion">ESP32-WROVER-B</span></td>
<td id="mwA1A">PCB trace</td>
<td id="mwA1E" rowspan="2" style="text-align:center">8</td>
<td id="mwA1I">Revision of ESP32-WROVER module with 8<span id="mwA1M" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MiB pSRAM (instead of 4<span id="mwA1Q" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MiB pSRAM) operating at 3.3V (instead of 1.8V in previous versions) and ESP32-D0WD (instead of ESP32-D0WDQ6). FCC part 15.247 tested (FCC ID 2AC7Z-ESP32WROVERB). Does not include U.FL connector. (Custom order option for flash capacity of 8<span id="mwA1U" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MiB or 16<span id="mwA1Y" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MiB also available.)</td></tr>
<tr id="mwA1c">
<td id="mwA1g"><span about="#mwt79" class="nowrap" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"nowrap","href":"./Template:Nowrap"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"ESP32-WROVER-IB"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwA1k" typeof="mw:Transclusion">ESP32-WROVER-IB</span></td>
<td id="mwA1o">U.FL socket, PCB trace</td>
<td id="mwA1s">Variation of ESP32-WROVER-B module configured to use an on-board U.FL compatible connector. PCB trace antenna not connected by default.</td></tr>
<tr id="mwA1w">
<td id="mwA10"><span about="#mwt80" class="nowrap" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"nowrap","href":"./Template:Nowrap"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"ESP32-WROVER-E"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwA14" typeof="mw:Transclusion">ESP32-WROVER-E</span></td>
<td id="mwA18">PCB trace</td>
<td id="mwA2A" rowspan="2" style="text-align:center">4,8,16</td>
<td id="mwA2E" rowspan="2" style="text-align:center">2,8</td>
<td id="mwA2I">Revision of ESP32-WROVER module with 2 or 8<span id="mwA2M" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MiB pSRAM (instead of 4<span id="mwA2Q" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MiB pSRAM) operating at 3.3V (instead of 1.8V in previous versions) and ESP32-D0WD-V3, or in 2MB pSRAM models, ESP32-D0WDR2-V3. FCC part 15.247 tested (FCC ID 2AC7Z-ESP32WROVERE). Does not include U.FL connector. (Custom order option for flash capacity of 2 MiB, 8<span id="mwA2U" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MiB, or 16<span id="mwA2Y" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MiB also available.)<sup about="#mwt83" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"EspressifESP32WROVEREDatasheet"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-EspressifESP32WROVEREDatasheet-21"}}' id="cite_ref-EspressifESP32WROVEREDatasheet_21-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e191" href="#cite_note-EspressifESP32WROVEREDatasheet-21" id="mwA2c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA2g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA2k">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA2o">]</span></span></a></sup></td></tr>
<tr id="mwA2s">
<td id="mwA2w"><span about="#mwt84" class="nowrap" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"nowrap","href":"./Template:Nowrap"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"ESP32-WROVER-IE"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwA20" typeof="mw:Transclusion">ESP32-WROVER-IE</span></td>
<td id="mwA24">U.FL socket, PCB trace</td>
<td id="mwA28">Variation of ESP32-WROVER-E module configured to use an on-board U.FL compatible connector. PCB trace antenna not connected by default.</td></tr>
<tr id="mwA3A">
<td id="mwA3E"><span about="#mwt85" class="nowrap" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"nowrap","href":"./Template:Nowrap"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"ESP32-PICO-V3-ZERO"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwA3I" typeof="mw:Transclusion">ESP32-PICO-V3-ZERO</span></td>
<td id="mwA3M">PCB trace</td>
<td id="mwA3Q" style="text-align:center">4</td>
<td id="mwA3U" style="text-align:center">0</td>
<td id="mwA3Y">Based on ESP32-PICO-V3 SiP. It is designed as a module for Alexa Connect Kit (ACK) and connecting with <a data-relay-id="e192" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Alexa" id="mwA3c" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Amazon Alexa">Amazon Alexa</a>.</td></tr>
<tr id="mwA3g">
<td id="mwA3k" rowspan="2">Ai-Thinker</td>
<td id="mwA3o">ESP32-S</td>
<td id="mwA3s">PCB trace</td>
<td id="mwA3w" style="text-align:center">4</td>
<td id="mwA30" style="text-align:center">0</td>
<td id="mwA34">Ai-Thinker's equivalent to Espressif's ESP-WROOM-32 module. (Same form factor and general specifications.)<sup about="#mwt88" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AIThinkerESP32SModule"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-AIThinkerESP32SModule-22"}}' id="cite_ref-AIThinkerESP32SModule_22-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e193" href="#cite_note-AIThinkerESP32SModule-22" id="mwA38"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA4A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA4E">[</span>22<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA4I">]</span></span></a></sup> Previously branded as "ESP-32S" with the hyphen before "32S", the initial release of the ESP-32S module replaced the previously announced, but never released, ESP3212 module.</td></tr>
<tr id="mwA4M">
<td id="mwA4Q">ESP32-A1S</td>
<td id="mwA4U">U.FL socket, PCB trace</td>
<td id="mwA4Y" style="text-align:center">8</td>
<td id="mwA4c" style="text-align:center">4</td>
<td id="mwA4g">Contains an extra AC101 audio codec IC whose IO-pins (line, mic, etc.) are led to the board pins. Comes separately or soldered onto a corresponding audio development board ("ESP32-Audio-Kit").<sup about="#mwt91" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"ESP32-A1S specs document"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-ESP32-A1S_specs_document-23"}}' id="cite_ref-ESP32-A1S_specs_document_23-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e194" href="#cite_note-ESP32-A1S_specs_document-23" id="mwA4k"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA4o"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA4s">[</span>23<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA4w">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt94" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Ai-Thinker ESP32 module overview"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Ai-Thinker_ESP32_module_overview-24"}}' id="cite_ref-Ai-Thinker_ESP32_module_overview_24-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e195" href="#cite_note-Ai-Thinker_ESP32_module_overview-24" id="mwA40"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA44"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA48">[</span>24<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA5A">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt97" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"ESP32-Audio Development Kit news"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-ESP32-Audio_Development_Kit_news-25"}}' id="cite_ref-ESP32-Audio_Development_Kit_news_25-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e196" href="#cite_note-ESP32-Audio_Development_Kit_news-25" id="mwA5E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA5I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA5M">[</span>25<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA5Q">]</span></span></a></sup></td></tr>
<tr id="mwA5U">
<td id="mwA5Y" rowspan="3">AnalogLamb</td>
<td id="mwA5c">ESP-32S-ALB</td>
<td id="mwA5g" rowspan="3">PCB trace</td>
<td id="mwA5k" style="text-align:center">4</td>
<td id="mwA5o" rowspan="2" style="text-align:center">0</td>
<td id="mwA5s">Clone of the ESP-32S module (ESP-WROOM-32 compatible footprint). Seen with a green solder mask coating.<sup about="#mwt100" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AnalogLambCloneModule"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-AnalogLambCloneModule-26"}}' id="cite_ref-AnalogLambCloneModule_26-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e197" href="#cite_note-AnalogLambCloneModule-26" id="mwA5w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA50"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA54">[</span>26<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA58">]</span></span></a></sup></td></tr>
<tr id="mwA6A">
<td id="mwA6E">ALB-WROOM</td>
<td id="mwA6I" style="text-align:center">16</td>
<td id="mwA6M">Variation of ESP-32S-ALB with 16 MiB of flash memory.<sup about="#mwt101" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"AnalogLambCloneModule"}}' id="cite_ref-AnalogLambCloneModule_26-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e198" href="#cite_note-AnalogLambCloneModule-26" id="mwA6Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA6U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA6Y">[</span>26<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA6c">]</span></span></a></sup></td></tr>
<tr id="mwA6g">
<td id="mwA6k">ALB32-WROVER</td>
<td id="mwA6o" style="text-align:center">4</td>
<td id="mwA6s" style="text-align:center">4</td>
<td id="mwA6w">ESP32 module board with 4<span id="mwA60" typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>MiB pSRAM with the same footprint as the ESP-WROOM-32 module.<sup about="#mwt104" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-27"}}' id="cite_ref-27" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e199" href="#cite_note-27" id="mwA64"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA68"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA7A">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA7E">]</span></span></a></sup></td></tr>
<tr id="mwA7I">

Also, footprint is unique and differs from all other ESP32 modules.<sup about="#mwt116" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"IteadPSHC32"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-IteadPSHC32-31"}}' id="cite_ref-IteadPSHC32_31-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e203" href="#cite_note-IteadPSHC32-31" id="mwA-c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA-g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA-k">[</span>31<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA-o">]</span></span></a></sup></td></tr>

<td id="mwBA8">PIFA</td>
<td id="mwBBA">Belongs to the u-blox NINA-W13 series of Wi-Fi modules.<sup about="#mwt123" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"ublox_NINA-W13-series"}}' id="cite_ref-ublox_NINA-W13-series_33-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e206" href="#cite_note-ublox_NINA-W13-series-33" id="mwBBE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBBI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBBM">[</span>33<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBBQ">]</span></span></a></sup> On board <a data-relay-id="e207" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverted-F_antenna#Planar_implementation" id="mwBBU" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Inverted-F antenna">planar inverted-F antenna</a> (PIFA) is shaped (cut & bent) metal, not a PCB trace.</td></tr>

Has 9 usable IO pins and microSD card slot.<sup about="#mwt149" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-40"}}' id="cite_ref-40" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e221" href="#cite_note-40" id="mwBHE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBHI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBHM">[</span>40<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBHQ">]</span></span></a></sup></td></tr>

<td id="mwBKs">Full-featured Arduino Uno-like development board compatible with Arduino Shields. It also adds additional SPI & IO pins. The board is a clone of WeMos D1 R32 with a USB Type B socket.</td></tr>
<tr id="mwBKw">
<td id="mwBK0">ESP32 DEVKIT V1</td>

</section><section aria-labelledby="Academic_uses" data-mw-section-id="12" id="mwBgo"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Academic_uses">Academic uses</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a data-relay-id="e298" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ESP32&action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section: Academic uses"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<ul id="mwBgs"><li id="mwBgw">ESP32 devices are utilized in educational settings<sup about="#mwt260" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-77"}}' id="cite_ref-77" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e299" href="#cite_note-77" id="mwBg0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBg4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBg8">[</span>77<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhA">]</span></span></a></sup> and academic research projects. Additionally, ESP32 is used in DIY projects such as building low-cost drones.<sup about="#mwt263" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-78"}}' id="cite_ref-78" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e300" href="#cite_note-78" id="mwBhE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBhI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhM">[</span>78<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhQ">]</span></span></a></sup>  The DJI Robomaster TT, an educational variant of the <a data-relay-id="e301" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryze_Tello" id="mwBhU" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="Ryze Tello">Ryze Tello</a> drone, is equipped with an ESP32.<sup about="#mwt266" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-79"}}' id="cite_ref-79" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e302" href="#cite_note-79" id="mwBhY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBhc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhg">[</span>79<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhk">]</span></span></a></sup></li></ul>
</section></section><section aria-labelledby="Undocumented_HCI_commands_in_ESP32" data-mw-section-id="13" id="mwBho"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Undocumented_HCI_commands_in_ESP32">Undocumented HCI commands in ESP32</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a data-relay-id="e303" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ESP32&action=edit&section=13" title="Edit section: Undocumented HCI commands in ESP32"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwBhs">In March 2025, researchers from Tarlogic Security identified undocumented Host Controller Interface (HCI) commands in the ESP32 Bluetooth firmware, prompting discussions about their functionality and potential implications.<sup about="#mwt269" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-80"}}' id="cite_ref-80" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e304" href="#cite_note-80" id="mwBhw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBh0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBh4">[</span>80<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBh8">]</span></span></a></sup> This discovery was presented on March 6, 2025, at the <a data-relay-id="e305" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RootedCON" id="mwBiA" rel="mw:WikiLink" title="RootedCON">RootedCON</a> conference by the Tarlogic Security team.<sup about="#mwt272" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-81"}}' id="cite_ref-81" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e306" href="#cite_note-81" id="mwBiE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBiI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBiM">[</span>81<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBiQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<p id="mwBiU">The identified commands, such as <i id="mwBiY">Write Memory</i> (0xFC02), are vendor-specific HCI commands used primarily for debugging and testing purposes. These types of commands are common in Bluetooth controller implementations to assist with development and troubleshooting. They are not part of the standard HCI command set and are typically used in controlled environments.<sup about="#mwt275" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-82"}}' id="cite_ref-82" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e307" href="#cite_note-82" id="mwBic"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBig"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBik">[</span>82<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBio">]</span></span></a></sup> While initially described as a "backdoor," further clarifications labeled them as "undocumented debugging features." These commands are not accessible remotely via standard Bluetooth connections but could be interacted with if an entity has physical access to the device or operates in an HCI-UART configuration.</p>
<p id="mwBis">Espressif Systems provided clarification regarding these commands, stating that they are intended for debugging and do not pose a security risk under normal operating conditions. The company emphasized that these commands cannot be triggered remotely and are not used in standard Bluetooth operations. These commands are present only in ESP32 chips and are not included in the ESP32-C, ESP32-S, and ESP32-H series. To address concerns raised within the security community, Espressif announced that future versions of the ESP-IDF would include updates to restrict access to these debugging commands and improve documentation for vendor-specific HCI commands. These actions aim to provide additional transparency and ensure developers are well-informed about available functionalities.<sup about="#mwt278" class="mw-ref reference" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-83"}}' id="cite_ref-83" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref"><a data-relay-id="e308" href="#cite_note-83" id="mwBiw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBi0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBi4">[</span>83<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBi8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
